overview.headline: Mach number controls air compressibility and density changes in flight

keyPoints.point: Low speed flight leaves air density constant, while higher speed compresses air locally
keyPoints.quote: If the aircraft passes at a low speed, typically less than 250 mph, it is observed that the density of the air remains constant.

keyPoints.point: Mach number compares aircraft speed to speed of sound in surrounding gas
keyPoints.quote: The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

keyPoints.point: Supersonic flows show density changes faster than velocity changes scaled by square
keyPoints.quote: For supersonic and hypersonic flows, the density changes faster than the velocity changes by a factor equal to the square of the Mach number.

keyPoints.point: Low subsonic conditions allow compressibility effects to be ignored
keyPoints.quote: For the low subsonic conditions, compressibility can be ignored.

keyTerms.gloss: ratio of aircraft speed to speed of sound in gas
keyTerms.quote: The Mach number is the ratio of the speed of the aircraft, or the speed of the gas, to the speed of sound in the gas.

keyTerms.gloss: effect that alters resulting force when air density changes
keyTerms.quote: This compressibility effect alters the amount of resulting force on the aircraft since the aerodynamic force depends on the air density.

keyTerms.quote: where a is equal to the speed of sound. So,
